subject.title: [Feature]: openclaw models status --probe --all — per-model health check across all configured models

question: Should OpenClaw add a core `models status --probe --all` live probe contract for every configured model, or fold this need into a broader model/fallback diagnostics workflow?
rationale: The missing behavior is source-proven, but it adds a new live CLI mode with token-cost, rate-limit, timeout, output-contract, and overlap implications that code inspection cannot choose alone.

options.title: Add the core CLI contract
options.body: Implement `models status --probe --all` in the existing status/probe path with clear provider/profile filtering, JSON output, docs, focused tests, and redacted live proof.

options.title: Fold into fallback diagnostics
options.body: Treat this as part of a broader fallback-chain/model-migration diagnostic workflow and keep this issue as design context until the canonical surface is chosen.

options.title: Defer live all-model probing
options.body: Keep current provider/auth probing and document manual or future alternatives if token cost and provider variance are not worth a core command now.

recommendation.title: Add the core CLI contract
recommendation.body: Implement `models status --probe --all` in the existing status/probe path with clear provider/profile filtering, JSON output, docs, focused tests, and redacted live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Most recent and repeated history in the model status/probe and provider identity paths makes this the strongest available product-routing owner.
